chunks: Aḥmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān and Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbbād al-Qaṣrī, both together from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said:
I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام): “May I be sacrificed for you, I have indeed grown old in age, so take my hand away from the Fire.”
He said: Then he gestured toward his son Abī al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) and said: “This is your master after me.”

key_terms.أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abū Ibrāhīm, the Imam addressed by the narrator
key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, identified here as the successor
key_terms.ابْنِهِ: His son, toward whom the Imam gestured
key_terms.النَّارِ: The Fire, referring to punishment in the afterlife
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: A reverential expression meaning: may I be sacrificed for you

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the Imamate of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā (عليه السلام) after Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith records a clear designation of Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) by Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) as the authority after him. The narrator, fearing the Fire in old age, seeks guidance for salvation, and the Imam directs him to his successor.
